title: PA: Anti-Union Halloween Trick
author: Peter Greene
summary: Greene responds to a Halloween flyer sent to Pennsylvania teachers by the Freedom Foundation, urging them to quit their union and 'take back' their paychecks. He situates the flyer within a broader network of anti-union groups funded by conservative foundations, whose stated aim is to defeat government unions as a political force. He traces the campaign back to the Janus decision and notes the repeated attempts to reach teachers at home. While admitting the state union sometimes errs, he argues that going without a union is like being your own lawyer, and that free-riding weakens the structure that protects everyone. His closing point is that teachers in states with gag laws are especially exposed without organized support. It is school-policy and profession commentary in his usual register.
points: The flyer is one move in a coordinated, well-funded campaign whose real goal is weakening teacher unions rather than helping teachers' paychecks.
Greene links the push directly to Janus and to repeated efforts to obtain teachers' home contact details.
His argument is practical: alternative associations do not match union representation and protection.
States where unions have been weakened show less job protection, lower pay and less professional voice.
Teacher gag laws make collective support more necessary for teachers facing public attacks.
quotes: Freedom Foundation is one of several active anti-union operations in the US. FF is all about fighting unions, specifically "government unions" who represent "a permanent lobby for bigger government.

The goal is to neutralize unions as a political force, specifically as a force to counter the "shrink government till it's small enough to drown in a bathtub crowd." The group's funders include the Bradley Foundation, the Charles Koch Foundation, and Searle Freedom Trust.

This kind of thing started roughly five seconds after the Supreme Court ruled on Janus, the case that established that members of government worker unions should not have to pay even a fair share. Groups like Freedom Foundation have filed numerous suits to get the home and email addresses of government employees, including teachers, precisely for this purpose.

But being your own union puts you on the same wisdom level as being your own lawyer. I'd love to live in a world in which management is so benevolent and altruistic that teachers don't need any representation; I would also love to live in a world in which I got back all my hair.

Getting people to quit the union is, first last and always, about weakening the union. If you think that would be great, simply look at the states where unions have been neutered--less job protection, les pay, less voice in the profession.

These are rough times to be without a union if you happen to be in a state with teacher gag laws that forbid you from mentioning sex, gender, race or "controversial topics"--and in a week or so, we'll learn which states are about to join that club. It would be a shame if a teacher had to face these kinds of attacks without any kind of organization to help support them.
